A B S T R A C T
Electroplating additives, especially levelers of copper electroplating, are the most critical components of elec-
troplating solutions in the manufacture of printed circuit boards and integrated circuits. A series of carbazole
derivatives have been synthesized and used as levelers for through-hole electroplating. Electrochemical tests,
theoretical calculations, and simulations were used to compare the various properties of the carbazole de
rivatives. Among them, the carbazole derivative Cz-BPDB was preferably subjected to electroplating which was
demonstrated by metallographic microscopy, SEM, and XRD. To further investigate the mechanism of leveler Cz-
BPDB, the nucleation model theory was used to explain the phenomenon of flat and smooth electroplating
surfaces. The electrostatic potential plot and the average local ionization energy plot were employed to analyze
the active sites of the Cz-BPDB. Moreover, the galvanostatic measurements were applied to investigate the
interaction of the Cz-BPDB with PEG and SPS. Therefore, a more reasonable through-hole electroplating
mechanism was proposed in electroplating solution with Cz-BPDB used as leveler. This work introduced an
excellent performance leveler and contributed to the continuing development of the copper electroplating
mechanism.

nologies, the miniaturization, lightweight, and high stability of various
smart devices are increasingly valued and required. In this context,
through-hole metallization in the manufacture of printed circuit boards
(PCBs) [1,2] and the packaging of integrated circuits (ICs) [3–5] is one
of the methods used to address the miniaturization of the devices.
Copper, a low-resistance and high-conductivity metal, is also used as a
through-hole metallization material for multilayer circuits to achieve
faster transmission of electrical signals [6]. Therefore, to realize the
metallization filling process of through holes, copper electroplating
technology is proposed and developed continuously [7–9].
At present, the acidic copper sulfate solution is more commonly used
for copper electroplating deposition [1], and the main components of
the Virgin Make-up Solution (VMS) are copper sulfate (CuSO<sub>4</sub>), sulfuric
acid (H SO ), and chloride ions (Cl<sup>−</sup> ) [10]. However, in through-hole

categories: inhibitors (i.e. polyethylene glycol (PEG) [13–15], poly-

[11,21–23], Diazine Black [24], Alcian Blue, Safranin T [25], 2-mercap-
topyridine [26,27], or 2,2-Dithiodipyridine [28]). With the synergistic
effect of the three additives, a bright and uniform thickness of the
electroplating inside and outside through hole is obtained. In previous
work, our group reported aliphatic amine organics [29–31] and large
conjugated molecules [32–39] as copper electroplating levelers, and all
of these levelers performed excellently.

In this work, a family of water-soluble carbazole derivatives were
synthesized in high yield. Electrochemical tests were employed to
explore the ability to inhibit the reduction and deposition of copper ions.
In theoretical calculations, molecular orbital calculations of carbazole
derivatives demonstrated the ability of carbazole derivatives to adsorb
onto copper surfaces. Furthermore, molecular dynamics simulations
visualized the adsorption behavior of carbazole derivatives on copper.
After through-hole electroplating experiments, the effect of compound
Cz-BPDB as a leveler was demonstrated by various instruments. Metal-
lographic microscopy was applied to test throwing power (TP) values.
SEM and XRD were respectively employed to observe the flatness of
electroplating surface and the dominant crystal orientation of electro-
plating layer. In addition, to investigate the mechanism of through-hole
electroplating, nucleation model theory, molecular properties, and
electrochemical properties were further analyzed. This work increased
the options for copper electroplating levelers with carbazole materials as
a new plating leveler and contributed to the continuing development of
the copper electroplating mechanism.
2. Material and methods
2.1. Materials synthesis and characterization
Five different compounds (Cz-TMA, Cz-PD, Cz-BPD, Cz-BPDM, and
Cz-BPDB) were synthesized via two- or three-step reaction using
commercially available carbazole as the starting substrate. The molec-
ular structures and synthesis routes of the five carbazole derivatives are
shown in Fig. 1. All the compounds obtained by synthesis were
confirmed to be the target products by <sup>1</sup>H NMR,<sup>13</sup>C NMR, and mass
spectrometry. (The corresponding spectra and data for carbazole de-
rivatives are shown in the Supporting Information.)
All reagents and chemicals in experiments were purchased from
commercial sources and used without further purification. All reactions
were monitored by TLC under UV light. <sup>1</sup>H NMR and <sup>13</sup>C NMR spectra
were recorded by a Bruker AVANCE III 400 spectrometer operating at
400 MHz and 101 MHz, respectively. High-resolution mass spectra
(HRMS) were obtained on a Xevo G2 TOF MS.
2.1.1. General procedure for the synthesis of compound Cz-Br
The reaction mixture of carbazole (0.1672 g, 1 mmol), 1,6-dibromo-
hexane (1.2199 g, 5 mmol), potassium hydroxide (0.1683 g, 3 mmol),
tetrabutylammonium bromide (0.3224 g, 1 mmol), and toluene (10 mL)
was kept stirring for 3 h with air condensation in 35 ◦C. And then, the
reaction solution was cooled to room temperature and stirred continu-
ously for 12 h. When carbazole was completely consumed as indicated
by TLC, the solvent was removed under reduced pressure. The crude
product was purified by column chromatography using silica gel (pe-
troleum ether and dichloromethane = 10:1–6:1, v/v) to give Cz-Br
(0.2673 g, 81 % yield) as a white solid.
2.1.2. General procedure for the synthesis of compound Cz-TMA
The reaction mixture of Cz-Br (0.3303 g, 1 mmol), trimethylamine
hydrochloride (0.4778 g, 5 mmol), sodium bicarbonate (0.42 g, 5
mmol), and acetonitrile (10 mL) was kept stirring for 12 h with Ar
protection in 80 ◦C. After the reaction was finished, the reaction was
cooled to room temperature. The solids in the reaction solution were
filtered to obtain the filtrate. The crude product in the filtrate was pu-
rified by column chromatography using neutral alumina (dichloro-
methane and methanol = 5:1, v/v) to give Cz-TMA (0.3422 g, 88 %
yield) as a white solid.
2.1.3. General procedure for the synthesis of compound Cz-PD
The reaction mixture of Cz-Br (0.3303 g, 1 mmol), pyridine (0.3955
g, 5 mmol), and acetonitrile (10 mL) was kept stirring for 24 h with Ar
protection at 80 ◦C. After the reaction was finished, the reaction was
cooled to room temperature. The reaction solution was poured into ethyl
acetate (150 mL) for recrystallization to obtain the product Cz-PD
(0.4038 g, 98 % yield) as a white solid.

4. Conclusions
In conclusion, the synthesized carbazole derivatives were used as
levelers for copper electroplating. Initially, Cz-BPDB was screened from
five carbazole derivatives as the most effective leveler by electro-
chemical and computational studies. Hereafter, various formulations
were designed to investigate the performance of Cz-BPDB. In Bath 5 with
0.5 ppm Cz-BPDB, the TP value of through-hole electroplating reached
104.77 %. Meanwhile, adding Cz-BPDB, the electroplating surface
became smooth and flat from roughness as seen by SEM. And after, the
dominant crystallographic orientation of the electroplating layer was
(111). Further, a series of works were carried out to investigate the
mechanism of action of Cz-BPDB. CA tests showed that the nucleation
pattern of the VPS + Cz-BPDB solution conformed to the instantaneous
nucleation model. The active sites of chemisorption and physisorption of
Cz-BPDB were analyzed and localized to the carbazole and pyridine
structures of Cz-BPDB in the ALIE plot and the ESP plot. Additionally,
the GMs test results illustrated the preferential adsorption sites of the
three additives in the electroplating through holes. Eventually, a
reasonable mechanism for through-hole electroplating is proposed,
which helps to promote the copper electroplating leveler to be further
investigated and developed.
